notes: Access: www.hay.com reached directly via HTTP (see na26.json notes for the us.hay.com/DWR redirect background and robots.txt check - no block encountered). Checked full Products mega-menu (Furniture/Lighting/Accessories and all sub-categories), footer nav, and homepage - no 'Bestsellers/Best Sellers/Top Sellers/Popular/Trending/Customer Favorites' entry anywhere in the consumer-facing shop navigation. Checked sitemap-content.xml (88KB, all non-product pages) and sitemap-products.xml (1407 product URLs) for 'best' /'popular'/'trending'/'favorite' URL patterns: the only hits were under /professionals/best-selling-products/ (a landing page + 7 category sub-pages: chairs, tables, sofas, storage, outdoor, lounge, lighting) and an unrelated case study /professionals/cases/bestseller (about the Danish fashion retailer 'Bestseller' headquarters project - not a merchandising page, confirmed by <title>HAY designs selected for Bestseller headquarters in Denmark</title>, excluded). Investigated /professionals/best-selling-products in full: it sits inside HAY's B2B 'Professionals'/trade microsite (alongside Cases, contract ordering info), not the general consumer Products catalogue. Its parent page (H1 'Best-selling products') is a landing grid of 8 tiles that mixes the 7 category links with one unrelated tile (/products/furniture/new-order-info, a furniture-care/ordering-info page) - i.e. it functions as a general Professionals info hub, not a dedicated Bestsellers index. Each of the 7 category sub-pages (chairs/tables/sofas/storage/outdoor/lounge/lighting) has the exact same fixed count of 4 tiles (verified by grepping div.mix-item on every sub-page) - a fixed curated-showcase template, not a real filterable/paginated PLP with a site-reported count. The tiles link to product families/collections (e.g. /hay/furniture/seating/chair/rey-chair, /sections/family/layout-armchair-and-chair) rather than to a SKU-level catalogue listing, and each page opens with marketing/editorial copy ('Chairs are at the heart of HAY's furniture collection...') before the 4-item grid. This fails the brief's test #1 (real PLP, not editorial/marketing) - it reads as a curated trade-audience showcase, not a genuine bestseller merchandising PLP, so it was excluded rather than recorded. Also ran the site's own search (Playwright, JS-rendered widget) for 'bestseller' and 'best seller' - the client-rendered search overlay did not resolve to a distinct results panel in the automated pass (inconclusive, not treated as proof of absence on its own), but combined with the exhaustive nav+sitemap check above this is sufficient to conclude no genuine consumer Bestsellers PLP exists on this site.
